newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal mixed on Brazil rumor, soyoil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal mixed on Brazil rumor, soyoil lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were mixed at midday with nearby contracts up on market talk that Brazil would impose an export tax on soybeans and soymeal, traders said.
Soyoil was weakened by the strength in soymeal and ideas supplies were sufficient to meet lackluster demand.

Floor sources said talk circulated Tuesday that Brazil would impose an export tax on soybeans and soymeal to curb the rapid export pace. But Brazil's agriculture ministry said in March it would oppose such a tax. Similar rumors cropped up on the trading floor in March.

"It is politically absurd and unviable," Favio Pereira, adviser at the ministry's Agricultural Policy Secretariat said in March, referring to the tax. "The Agriculture Ministry is opposed to the idea, clearly opposed."

New crop months were pressured by ideas U.S. soybean plantings were progressing well depsite a cool, damp spring. USDA on Monday said nine percent of the U.S. soybean crop was seeded as of Sunday, above trade expectations.
At 1211 CDT, soymeal was up $0.80 per ton to down $2.50 with July up $0.20 at $290.00. Soyoil was down 0.21 cent per lb to unchanged with July down 0.11 at 25.05.
